# Ducky: MIDI implementation

Ducky talks to a host over the Seed's USB MIDI port with SysEx, and takes two Control Changes: CC 11 (Expression) moves the EXP control and CC 102 selects a preset (Controls). It plays no notes, follows no clock and never sends CC. The protocol table in `daisy/src/link.h` is the single source of truth; this file is generated from it. `bun tools/pedal.ts` is the command-line client (`editor/src/link/` holds the protocol code it shares with the editor).

## Framing

- Every message except the Identity pair is `F0 7D 64 01 <cmd> <payload> F7`: manufacturer `7D` (non-commercial), device `64`, protocol version `01`. SysEx for other devices and other versions is ignored.
- Integers travel as 7-bit bytes (septets), most significant first: u14 is 2 bytes, u21 3, u28 4, u32 5 (the top septet holds bits 28-31).
- Binary data travels as Pack7: each group of up to 7 bytes becomes one header byte followed by the low 7 bits of each byte; bit i of the header is the most significant bit of the group's byte i. n bytes pack into n + ceil(n/7). Example: `80 01 FF 7F 00 81 42 C3` packs to `25 00 01 7F 7F 00 01 42 01 43`.
- The CRC is CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3 / zlib: reflected polynomial EDB88320, initial and final XOR FFFFFFFF), the same as the model and preset binaries'.
- Limits: an UPLOAD CHUNK carries at most 256 bytes (293 packed), so the longest host -> pedal message is 307 bytes; pedal -> host payloads are at most 200 bytes (a LOG line at most 120, each SLOT name at most 63).
- The pedal handles one request at a time: send the next request after the previous one's RESULT. Slot numbers are 0-7 on the wire (the pedal's log and `tools/pedal.ts` count 1-8).

## Commands

|Direction|Command|Payload|Effect|
|---|---|---|---|
|host to pedal|Identity Request|`F0 7E <id> 06 01 F7` (Universal Non-Real-Time, any id 00-7F)|The pedal answers the Identity Reply.|
|pedal to host|Identity Reply|`F0 7E 7F 06 02 7D 64 00 <board> 00 <flags> 00 00 00 <build id> F7`|Manufacturer 7D, family 64 00 (the device byte 64, then 00), member `<board>` 00 (1 HotHouse, 2 BurningBungalow), version `<flags>` 00 00 00: bit 0 set when the image plays the weight morph (the weight build, `APP=weight`), clear for the xfade build (the default) and the images without a morph; then the build id: 1-32 printable ASCII bytes, the short git commit with `+dirty` when tracked files differ (e.g. `711fa7c+dirty`), or `unknown` outside git.|
|host to pedal|Control Change 11 (Expression)|`Bn 0B <value 0-127>` (n: the channel - 1; running status accepted)|Moves EXP, the expression pedal control, to value / 127 when the channel matches EXP CHANNEL's (the Seed's USB MIDI port) or, on a BurningBungalow, MIDI IN CHANNEL's (its MIDI IN jack) (Controls). Other CCs (but CC 102), notes and other channel messages are ignored. No RESULT, no log line.|
|host to pedal|Control Change 102 (Preset)|`Bn 66 <value 0-7>` (n: the channel - 1; running status accepted)|Switches to slot value + 1 when the channel matches EXP CHANNEL's (the Seed's USB MIDI port) or, on a BurningBungalow, MIDI IN CHANNEL's (its MIDI IN jack): the switch FS2 makes (fade out, load, fade in; LED2 blinks the slot; the state record 2 s later), and the `preset` line. The playing slot restarts LED2's blinks only. A value of 8 or more, or a slot that is not ok, is ignored and logged: `preset cc V ignored`, `preset cc V ignored: slot N STATUS`. No RESULT.|
|host to pedal|`01` HELLO|none|The pedal answers with LOG lines: the boot line `ducky <board> seed <version> sysclk N MHz audio N Hz N bit block N <build id>`, then the `slots`, `preset`, `model`, `ir`, `gate`, `morph`, `settings`, `layout`, `exp`, `pedal` (a BurningBungalow only) and `loop` lines (docs/FIRMWARE.md "Log lines"). No RESULT.|
|host to pedal|`02` LIST|none|8 SLOT messages (slots 0-7), then RESULT `02` ok with value 8.|
|host to pedal|`03` ERASE|`<slot 0-7>`|Erases the slot (it reads empty afterwards). RESULT ok with the flash time in ms.|
|host to pedal|`04` RENAME|`<slot 0-7> <name: 1-63 bytes 20-7E>`|Rewrites the preset's name (and its CRC); the model and the IR are kept. RESULT ok with the flash time in ms; `slot-state` when the slot is not ok.|
|host to pedal|`05` SWAP|`<a 0-7> <b 0-7>` (a != b)|Exchanges the two slots' contents (either may be empty). RESULT ok with the flash time in ms; `slot-state` when either slot is neither ok nor empty.|
|host to pedal|`06` DFU|none|The pedal logs `dfu reset` and restarts into the Daisy bootloader's DFU mode (no timeout), ready for tools/flash_when_ready.sh. No RESULT.|
|host to pedal|`07` WATCH|`<on 0/1>`|RESULT ok (value 0). While on, a STATUS and a VALUES every 100 ms, the first 100 ms after WATCH on. Off at boot.|
|host to pedal|`08` UPLOAD BEGIN|`<slot 0-7> <size u21>` (a preset image's size: Upload)|Starts staging a preset image for the slot, discarding any earlier upload. RESULT value: the next offset (0). `bad-request` when the size is not one a preset image has.|
|host to pedal|`09` UPLOAD CHUNK|`<offset u21> <crc32 u32> <Pack7 data>` (1-256 bytes unpacked; the CRC-32 of the unpacked data)|Stages the data at offset. RESULT value: the next expected offset. A resent chunk (offset below it) is accepted again; an offset past it answers `offset`.|
|host to pedal|`0A` UPLOAD COMMIT|none|Validates the complete image as a preset, writes it to its slot and verifies the flash; the upload is cleared whatever the outcome. RESULT ok with the flash time in ms; `invalid` with the slot status number (Slot status) when the image does not parse, or with `morph` when its morph block targets the slot it is uploaded to. The target slot is not checked otherwise: the pedal looks for the model the block names when the preset loads.|
|host to pedal|`1B` FIRMWARE BEGIN|`<size u21> <crc32 u32>` (a firmware image's size, 1040-491520 bytes, and the CRC-32 of the whole image)|Starts staging a firmware image, discarding any earlier one. RESULT value: the next offset (0). `bad-request` when the size is out of range or the payload is not 8 bytes.|
|host to pedal|`1C` FIRMWARE CHUNK|`<offset u21> <crc32 u32> <Pack7 data>` (1-256 bytes unpacked; the CRC-32 of the unpacked data)|As UPLOAD CHUNK, for the firmware image.|
|host to pedal|`1D` FIRMWARE COMMIT|none|Checks the complete image (Firmware update), erases the firmware's QSPI blocks from 0x90040000, writes the image and reads it back. RESULT ok with the flash time in ms; the pedal then logs `firmware restart` and restarts into the new image. `invalid` with the failed check (Firmware checks) clears the staged image; `flash` keeps it, so COMMIT can be sent again: the running firmware is untouched until a restart.|
|host to pedal|`0B` READ|`<slot 0-7> <offset u21>`|Reads up to 160 bytes of the slot's preset image from offset: one DATA, then RESULT ok with the next offset (offset + the bytes sent). `bad-request` when the payload is not 4 bytes, the slot is not 0-7 or the offset is at or past the image's size; `slot-state` when the slot is not ok. Reads flash only: audio and the slot are untouched.|
|host to pedal|`0C` GATE|`<slot 0-7> <enabled 0/1> <threshold 30-80> <attack 5-100> <hold 10-100> <release u14 10-1000> <ratio 15-100>`|Rewrites the preset's noise-gate block (and its CRC); the model, the IR and the name are kept. Threshold in dB below full scale (the gate closes below it and opens 6 dB above it), attack in 0.1 ms, hold and release in ms (release: the time to fall 60 dB), ratio (the expander's) in tenths. When the slot is playing, the gate takes the settings at once, with no reload. RESULT ok with the flash time in ms; `slot-state` when the slot is not ok.|
|host to pedal|`0D` GATE TRY|`<slot 0-7> <enabled 0/1> <threshold 30-80> <attack 5-100> <hold 10-100> <release u14 10-1000> <ratio 15-100>`|Sets the running gate only, until the next preset load or GATE; nothing is written. RESULT ok (value 0); `slot-state` when the slot is not the playing one.|
|host to pedal|`0E` DUMP|none|One PARAM per parameter (ids 0 to N-1), one VALUES, then RESULT ok with N.|
|host to pedal|`0F` SET|`<id> <code u14>`|Sets the parameter's value from the next audio block (continuous: code / 16383 along its taper; choice: the index). Every control on it is held until it moves (a knob more than 3 % of its travel, a switch to another position). RESULT ok with the code taken (clamped). `bad-request` for a payload other than 3 bytes or an unknown id. No log line.|
|host to pedal|`10` ASSIGN|`<control 0-8> <id, or 7F none>`|Puts the parameter on the control (0-3 Knobs 3-6, 4-6 SW1-SW3, 7 EXP, the expression pedal over MIDI, 8 PEDAL, a BurningBungalow's expression pedal jack); it keeps its value until the control moves. Logs `assign CONTROL NAME`. RESULT ok (value 0). `bad-request` for a payload other than 2 bytes, a control past 8, an unknown id, a continuous parameter on a switch, or control 8 on a HotHouse.|
|host to pedal|`11` SAVE|none|Writes the assignments, the expression and MIDI IN channels and every parameter's value to the settings record, used at the next power-up. Logs `settings seq N T ms`. RESULT ok with the flash time in ms; `flash` when the write fails (`settings write failed`).|
|host to pedal|`19` MORPH|`<slot 0-7>` (clear) or `<slot 0-7> <Pack7 64-byte morph block>` (docs/FIRMWARE.md "Preset store")|Rewrites the preset's morph block (and its CRC), or removes it; the model, the IR, the name and the gate are kept, and the waypoints of a trained path the preset had are removed: the block set is a straight blend. The block's target slot must be ok, hold the model whose CRC the block names, and not be the slot itself. On the playing slot the preset reloads, with the preset-switch fade. RESULT ok with the flash time in ms; `bad-request` for a payload of another length, a block that does not parse (target, permutation, scales, matrix, fits) or one that targets its own slot; `slot-state` when the slot or the target is not ok, or the target's model is not the block's.|
|host to pedal|`1A` EXP CHANNEL|`<channel 0-16>`|Sets the MIDI channel EXP's CC 11 and the preset CC 102 are taken from on the Seed's USB MIDI port: 0 any channel (omni, the factory setting), 1-16 that channel. Acts at once; SAVE keeps it. Logs `exp channel omni|N`. RESULT ok (value 0). `bad-request` for a payload other than 1 byte or a channel past 16.|
|host to pedal|`1E` MIDI IN CHANNEL|`<channel 0-16>`|A BurningBungalow's MIDI IN jack: sets the MIDI channel CC 11 (EXP) and CC 102 (preset) are taken from on it: 0 any channel (omni, the factory setting), 1-16 that channel. Acts at once; SAVE keeps it. Logs `midi in channel omni|N`. RESULT ok (value 0). `bad-request` for a payload other than 1 byte, a channel past 16, or on a HotHouse.|
|pedal to host|`12` LOG|`<printable ASCII, at most 120 bytes>`|One log line (boot, HELLO, slot and control changes, the controls and status lines once a second).|
|pedal to host|`13` SLOT|`<slot 0-7> <status> <flags> <preset name> 00 <model name> 00 <ir name>`|One slot, answering LIST. Status: Slot status. Flags: bit 0 has an IR, bit 1 playing. Names: printable ASCII of at most 63 bytes (anything else becomes `?`); all three are empty unless the status is ok, the IR name is empty without an IR.|
|pedal to host|`14` RESULT|`<cmd> <code> <value u21>`|The outcome of a request (Results). Every request except HELLO and DFU gets exactly one RESULT, and it comes last.|
|pedal to host|`15` STATUS|`<load avg u14> <load max u14> <underruns u28> <slot> <mute> <knob 1-6: 6 x u14> <SW1> <SW2> <SW3> <footswitches> <gate level u14> <gate cut u14> <comp cut u14> <pedal u14>` (34 bytes)|Sent every 100 ms while WATCH is on. Load in permille, as the last once-a-second `load` line reported it (0 before the first); underruns since boot, clamped at 2^28 - 1; slot 0-7, or 7F when dry; mute 0/1; knobs in permille (0-1000); SW1-SW3 0 down, 1 middle, 2 up; footswitches held: bit 0 FS1, bit 1 FS2. Gate level: the highest level the gate's detector saw at the input (before the compressor and Knob 1) since the previous STATUS, in tenths of a dB below full scale (0-1200, 1200 for silence); gate cut: the largest gain reduction the gate applied since the previous STATUS, in tenths of a dB (0-1200, 1200 closed); comp cut: the largest reduction of the compressor's low-frequency gain below Sustain's since the previous STATUS, in tenths of a dB (0-1200; 0 when the compressor is off); pedal: the expression jack's travel in permille (0-1000), 0 on a HotHouse.|
|pedal to host|`16` DATA|`<slot 0-7> <offset u21> <crc32 u32> <Pack7 data>` (1-160 bytes unpacked)|Answers READ: the image bytes at offset and the CRC-32 of the unpacked bytes. Comes before READ's RESULT.|
|pedal to host|`17` PARAM|`<id> <taper> <off end> <default u14> <min f32 as u32> <max f32 as u32> <name> 00 <label> 00 <unit> 00 <group>`|One parameter (Parameters), answering DUMP. Taper: 0 log (continuous: the value runs from min at code 0 to max at code 16383, logarithmically), 1 choice (the value is an index 0 to max), 2 linear (the value runs from min at code 0 to max at code 16383, linearly). Off end: 0 none, 1 the parameter's filter is bypassed within 2 % of min, 2 within 2 % of max. Default: the value's code. Min and max: IEEE 754 single-precision bits. The strings are printable ASCII: the name is the log's and `tools/pedal.ts`'s, the label the editor's; a choice's unit is its labels, comma-separated, in index order.|
|pedal to host|`18` VALUES|`<control 0-8 assignments: 9 bytes> <held bits u14> <exp channel> <midi in channel> <N> <code u14 x N>`|The live assignments (7F none), bit s of held set while control s is held, the expression channel and the MIDI IN channel (0 any, 1-16), and each parameter's code. After DUMP's PARAMs, and with every STATUS while WATCH is on.|

## Results

RESULT's value: the next expected offset for UPLOAD BEGIN and CHUNK and FIRMWARE BEGIN and CHUNK; for READ the next offset; for COMMIT the flash time in ms on ok, the slot status on `invalid`, else 0; for FIRMWARE COMMIT the flash time in ms on ok, the Firmware check on `invalid`, else 0; for ERASE, RENAME, SWAP, GATE, MORPH and SAVE the flash time in ms on ok, else 0; 8 for LIST; the parameter count for DUMP; the code taken for SET; 0 for WATCH, GATE TRY, ASSIGN and EXP CHANNEL. A LIST, WATCH, COMMIT, FIRMWARE COMMIT, DUMP or SAVE with a payload of the wrong length answers `bad-request`.

|Code|Name|Meaning|
|---|---|---|
|0|ok|Done.|
|1|bad-request|Wrong payload length or a field out of range (slot, size, a firmware size, name, a == b, chunk data past the image, bad Pack7, a gate field, a parameter or control field, a morph block, an EXP CHANNEL or MIDI IN CHANNEL channel, ASSIGN of PEDAL or MIDI IN CHANNEL on a HotHouse).|
|2|no-upload|UPLOAD or FIRMWARE CHUNK or COMMIT without its BEGIN (or after a COMMIT that cleared it).|
|3|offset|The chunk's offset is past the next expected offset (the value); resend from there.|
|4|crc|The chunk's data does not match its CRC; resend it.|
|5|incomplete|COMMIT before every byte of the image was received.|
|6|invalid|COMMIT: the image does not parse as a preset, or its morph block targets its own slot (the value is the slot status); FIRMWARE COMMIT: the image fails a check (the value is the Firmware check).|
|7|flash|The flash erase, write or read-back failed.|
|8|slot-state|The slot's state does not allow it (RENAME, GATE or MORPH of a slot that is not ok, SWAP of a corrupt slot, GATE TRY of a slot that is not playing, MORPH to a target that is not ok or holds another model).|

## Slot status

SLOT's status byte and an `invalid` COMMIT's value: the slot parser's verdict (daisy/src/preset.h, docs/FIRMWARE.md "Preset store").

|Value|Name|
|---|---|
|0|ok|
|1|empty|
|2|magic|
|3|version|
|4|size|
|5|crc|
|6|model|
|7|ir|
|8|morph|

## Controls

- Controls 0-8 are Knob 3, Knob 4, Knob 5, Knob 6, SW1, SW2, SW3, EXP, the expression pedal over MIDI, and PEDAL, a BurningBungalow's expression pedal jack (`k3`-`k6`, `sw1`-`sw3`, `exp`, `pedal` in the log and `tools/pedal.ts`). Each drives one parameter or none (7F); a parameter may be on several controls or on none. Knobs 1 and 2 are fixed: the input trim and the output volume. A HotHouse has no PEDAL: ASSIGN of control 8 answers bad-request and a saved PEDAL assignment is ignored.
- A knob takes any parameter. A choice parameter on a knob splits its travel evenly between its values, and changes 0.05 of a step past each boundary, so a knob resting on one does not flip.
- A switch takes choice parameters only. A three-value parameter's index is the position: 0 down, 1 middle, 2 up. A two-value one is 0 in the middle and 1 up or down.
- EXP takes any parameter, as a knob does. Its position is the last CC 11 (Expression) value / 127 received on the Seed's USB MIDI port, e.g. from a USB-MIDI expression pedal acting as USB host, on the channel EXP CHANNEL sets, or on a BurningBungalow's MIDI IN jack on the channel MIDI IN CHANNEL sets (any channel unless set). Each CC writes the parameter; until the first one after power-up the parameter keeps its saved value.
- PEDAL takes any parameter, as a knob does, and writes it every block from the jack: the reading from 0.03 (heel) to 0.92 (toe) of the ADC's range spread over the travel (controls.h PedalTravel). An empty jack reads about 4 %, about 1 % of travel: there is no plug detection.
- Presets: CC 102 with value 0-7 switches to slot 1-8, as FS2 does, on EXP CHANNEL's channel on the USB MIDI port or MIDI IN CHANNEL's on a BurningBungalow's MIDI IN jack; a value past the slots, or an empty or broken slot, is ignored.
- Pickup: a control writes its parameter when it moves. SET, and ASSIGN of a control, hold the control: the parameter keeps its value until a knob, EXP or PEDAL has moved more than 3 % of its travel from where it was, or a switch changes position. When a parameter is on several controls, the one moved last has it and the others are held. VALUES' held bits show the held controls.
- At power-up every parameter on a knob, a switch or PEDAL takes its control's position (with several controls on it, one of theirs); one on EXP or on no control takes its saved value.
- ASSIGN and SET act at once but are lost at power-off. SAVE writes the assignments, the expression and MIDI IN channels and the values to the settings record (docs/FIRMWARE.md "Settings record"); with no record the pedal starts in the factory layout with every parameter at its default. The settings are global: presets hold neither assignments nor values.
- Factory layout (params.h kFactoryAssign): `k3` `bell2_gain`, `k4` `low_cut_freq`, `k5` `high_cut_freq`, `k6` `comp_balance`, `sw1` `low_cut_slope`, `sw2` `comp_mode`, `sw3` `comp_level`, `exp` `none`, `pedal` `none`.

## Upload

An image is a complete format-3 preset slot (docs/FIRMWARE.md "Preset store"): 7996 bytes without an IR, 16288 with one; 64 more with a morph block, and 7480 more for each of its trained path's waypoints (0-3), 38792 at most. UPLOAD BEGIN takes these sizes only. An upload replaces the whole slot, so one without a morph block over a preset drops the block and the waypoints it had; MORPH sets or removes the block of a stored preset, and removes its waypoints.

1. UPLOAD BEGIN `<slot> <size>`; RESULT ok, value 0. A BEGIN discards any earlier upload. Resend it when no RESULT arrives.
2. UPLOAD CHUNK for each run of up to 256 bytes, in order: `<offset> <crc> <data>`. RESULT ok gives the next offset. With no RESULT (1 s) or `crc`, resend the same chunk: a chunk at or below the next offset is accepted again, so resending is safe. `offset` (the chunk starts past the next expected offset) gives the offset to continue from. `tools/pedal.ts` gives up after 5 retries of one chunk.
3. UPLOAD COMMIT: the pedal parses the image as a preset, erases the slot's 64 KB block, writes the image and reads it back. The upload is cleared whatever the outcome, so COMMIT is not resent: with no RESULT (allow 10 s), LIST shows whether the slot holds the new preset.

## Firmware update

The image is the `.bin` of an `APP=xfade` (the default) or `APP=weight` build (`daisy/build/<board>-*/ducky_*.bin`, `<board>` hothouse or burningbungalow), 1040-491520 bytes. The Daisy bootloader copies it from QSPI 0x90040000 into SRAM 0x24000000 at boot, so the running firmware never executes from the flash it rewrites. It starts with the vector table; at 0x400 it carries a 16-byte tag: `DKFW` (0x57464B44 little-endian), version 1, the board (the Identity Reply's), the Identity Reply's flags, each a little-endian u32 (`daisy/src/fw_image.h`). Images without the tag (the `APP=bench` and `APP=latency` builds, and builds made before firmware updates) are refused: every image that is accepted can itself be updated this way. `tools/pedal.ts firmware FILE.bin` and the editor's Firmware button run these steps.

1. FIRMWARE BEGIN `<size> <crc>`, the CRC-32 of the whole image; RESULT ok, value 0. A BEGIN discards any earlier image.
2. FIRMWARE CHUNK for each run of up to 256 bytes, as UPLOAD CHUNK (Upload), with the same resends.
3. FIRMWARE COMMIT (allow 30 s): the pedal checks the image (Firmware checks), erases the 64 KB blocks it covers from 0x90040000, writes it and reads it back, then answers RESULT ok with the flash time; audio keeps running meanwhile. Resend COMMIT only on `flash`, which keeps the staged image. The pedal then logs `firmware restart` and restarts through the bootloader into the new image (audio stops for a few seconds); it comes back on USB with the new Identity, its presets and settings untouched.

## Firmware checks

An `invalid` FIRMWARE COMMIT's value, in the order the pedal checks: the image's CRC-32 is BEGIN's; its initial stack pointer lies in DTCM and its reset vector is a Thumb address inside the image as loaded in SRAM; the tag's magic and version; the tag's board is the pedal's. Nothing is erased when a check fails, and the staged image is cleared.

|Value|Name|
|---|---|
|0|ok|
|1|crc|
|2|vectors|
|3|tag|
|4|board|

## Slot changes and playback

- Audio keeps running through every slot operation: the audio callback reads nothing from QSPI. Each flash operation blocks the pedal's main loop for its erase and write (hundreds of ms): LOG lines, STATUS and footswitch preset switches wait, then catch up.
- Every successful slot change logs a line (`upload slot N "NAME" T ms`, `erase slot N T ms`, `rename slot N "NAME" T ms`, `swap slots A B T ms`, `gate slot N on|off T ms`, `morph slot N -> M|off T ms`), then the `slots` line; a failed write logs `slot write failed N`.
- An upload into the playing slot reloads it at once, with the usual preset-switch fade. An upload while the pedal plays dry (no valid slot) starts playing the new slot.
- Erasing the playing slot switches to the next filled slot (LED2 blinks its number), or to dry when none is left. A rename leaves the audio untouched.
- GATE on the playing slot changes the running gate at once, without a reload or a fade. GATE TRY changes only the running gate, so an editor can audition settings while a slider moves; the next preset load (a footswitch switch, an upload, an erase) or GATE undoes it.
- MORPH on the playing slot reloads it, with the preset-switch fade. A playing preset whose morph target is uploaded over, erased or swapped reloads too: it goes on morphing with whichever slot holds the model its block was fitted to, and plays its own model alone when none does (the log's `morph missing slot N`). An uploaded preset's morph block is resolved the same way, so it may arrive before its target.
- SWAP moves presets, not playback: the playing preset keeps playing under its new slot number, which the pedal remembers (as after a footswitch switch, once it has settled for 2 s). SWAP writes slot a, then slot b: a power loss between the two writes leaves both slots holding b's old preset, or both empty when b was empty (a's preset is lost); LIST shows it, and an upload restores it.
